title: Security claims attack-matrix and sell language
content:
Purpose and intended audience:

This is a working GTM brief combining: 1) an "attack matrix" of typical security/compliance buyer objections, 2) direct evidence tiers we can surface quickly, and 3) short, prescriptive sales language and demo hooks for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/Ops conversations. Audience: AE/SEs, CSEs, and growth marketers crafting one-pagers for enterprise opportunities.

High-level positioning to use up-front (30–60s):
- Topline: "Redwood Inference provides a production-grade inference platform with explicit auditability and configurable data protection controls — designed so your security team gets verifiable telemetry and your compliance team can map controls to SOC2/ISO/HIPAA."
- Quick differentiator: "We combine a high-performance runtime with curated audit artifacts (long retention, structured event traces, and canned control mappings) so you don’t trade observability for throughput."

Attack matrix: common buyer concerns, root cause, recommended evidence + tight rebuttal lines

1) Concern: "We need full audit trail for every inference (who/what/when)."
- Root cause: Security wants deterministic answers for incident forensics and vendor risk reviews.
- Evidence to prepare: sample audit export (CSV + JSON) of inference events, retention policy note, schema of events (user_id, api_key_id, model_version, request_payload_hash, response_meta, latency_ms, node_id, region, timestamp).
- Rebuttal language: "We capture per-request structured events (not just free-form logs). We can export a self-contained audit bundle that maps tokens and model versions to customer request IDs and request/response hashes for cryptographic verification."

2) Concern: "How is customer data isolated and retained in the hosted product?"
- Root cause: Legal/priv teams worry about data residency, retention, and third-party processing.
- Evidence: Data flow description (ingress->queue->runtime->KV cache->ephemeral storage->metrics sink), retention options (7/30/90/365 days), and contractual artifact language (DPA excerpt).
- Rebuttal: "Hosted customers can opt into dedicated-private paths: retention windows are configurable per-account and we support VPC peering or Private deployments for regulated workloads. For hosted we offer per-customer keying and configurable KV cache eviction policies."

3) Concern: "HIPAA — is PHI ever persisted or processed in a way that violates BAA terms?"
- Root cause: Customer must ensure vendor’s processing model and administrative safeguards meet BAA obligations.
- Evidence: BAA draft, high-level technical controls (access controls, encryption-at-rest and -in-transit, HSM/KMS integration), and a sample incident response runbook.
- Rebuttal: "We support signing a BAA and provide private deployment options. When PHI must be processed in-hosted mode, we recommend Dedicated deployments with SSE-KMS + audit log retention >365 days."

4) Concern: "SOC2/ISO mapping — show me controls you cover and what we need to own."
- Root cause: Risk teams want explicit responsibility matrix.
- Evidence: Two-column controls map (what Redwood provides vs customer responsibilities) for common SOC2/ISO controls: access mgmt, logging, change control, vendor mgmt, encryption, incident mgmt. Also include sample SOC2 auditor-friendly evidence (control IDs + artifact names).
- Rebuttal: "We provide pre-mapped artifacts for common SOC2 controls (e.g., log exports, change logs for model deployments, test results for backup/restore). We’re explicit about shared responsibilities in the customer onboarding pack."

Competitive notes (what different vendors emphasize / weak spots to call out):
- Major cloud providers: emphasize tenancy isolation and global compliance footprint; weaknesses: opaque inference telemetry, higher per-token telemetry cost for long tail.
- Managed LLM APIs (pure hosted): emphasize simplicity; weaknesses: limited retention choices, few canned auditor artifacts, and they often lack per-request structured event exports.
- Self-hosted runtimes/vendors: emphasize control and air-gapped options; weaknesses: heavy ops burden and few turnkey audit artifacts for auditors.
- Redwood play: emphasize balanced tradeoff — turnkey artifacts + migration path to Dedicated/Private with minimal app changes.

Three-tier evidence pack for sales (include in every enterprise POC):
- Tier 1 (instant): pre-canned PDF cheat-sheet + one-page DPA excerpt + sample audit export (anonymized) for quick validation by security screeners.
- Tier 2 (coordinated): SOC2 snapshot (if available), control mapping spreadsheet, and short recorded demo showing export creation and filtering in Console.
- Tier 3 (engaged): on-demand sandbox with extended retention, S3/Glacier export of logs, and SE-led run-through for compliance team questions.

Recommended audit-log claim language (short, use in PRDs / SOWs / one-pagers):
- "Per-request structured audit events retained for configurable windows (7/30/90/365 days) and exportable as verifiable JSON/CSV bundles for third-party audit."
- "Retention, export, and deletion policies are configurable per-account and can be enforced via policy + cryptographic request hashes for tamper-evidence."

Messaging snippets for AEs (quick copy-paste):
- Initial reply to security screener: "We capture structured per-request telemetry and provide a built-for-audit export. I’ve attached a 1-page sample and the DPA excerpt — happy to schedule a 30-min technical review with our SE."
- Demo opener for compliance reviewers: "We’ll show two things: the live audit export for a single request, and the controls map showing what Redwood provides vs what your team retains responsibility for."

Short demo script (10–12 minutes):
1) 90s: Platform overview emphasizing telemetry-first design.
2) 3 min: Console — show request search, drill into a request, and export.
3) 3 min: Show retention config and example automated export to S3.
4) 2 min: Show BAA/DPA attachment and where control artifacts live.
5) 60s: Q&A and next steps (sandbox + SE deep-dive).

Objection handling quick hits:
- "We require on-prem only": "We support on-prem and VPC/private deployments — we can show how the data plane looks identical to hosted while giving you network-level isolation and customer-managed keys."
- "We need longer retention than hosted offers": "We can provide extended retention inside Dedicated/Private and automated export to your S3 for archival."

Open items / decisions needed from product/legal before we finalize seller kit:
- Minimum artifact export schema (final field names and required hashes).
- Default retention tiers and pricing impact for the hosted product.
- Template BAA language and escalation path for incident reporting.

Next steps (owner + timeline):
- SEs to validate sample audit export format with internal infra (Evan Soto) — due 2025-10-09.
- Legal to produce BAA template mark-up (Maya Rodriguez) — due 2025-10-15.
- Create the Tier 1 PDF pack and attach to partner portal (Priya Nair) — due 2025-10-22.

Notes and references:
- Keep exports structured (avoid freeform text) — auditors prefer columnar fields they can map to control IDs.
- When in doubt: offer a sandbox with extended retention and SE-assisted walk-through rather than over-promising a hosted config change.

This is a working draft — comments inline welcome. Use this doc to spin the one-pager and the AE cheat-sheet.
